newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Drought fears keep Colombo rubber prices buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Drought fears keep Colombo rubber prices buoyant.

text.p: Strong demand fuelled by fears of a drop in output later this month due to dry weather kept prices up at Friday's rubber auctions, brokers said.

"Despite the good January crop, prices rose on fears that there may be a shortfall later in February due to drought in growing areas and wintering," said Upali Bandaranayake of brokers Forbes & Walker.
Prices of better grades rose between 1.25 rupees and 1.75 rupees a kilo, at the auction where 297 tonnes of latex, 67 tonnes of scrap and 18 tonnes of sheet, were on offer.
Best latex one-x, the purest grade, rose to 73.50 rupees per kilo from 72 rupees last week.
Number one fetched 72.50 rupees per kilo, from 71 rupees.
RSS 1 was not quoted, Bandaranayake said.
The auction, which was scheduled for Thursday was held on Friday because of a public holiday earlier in the week.
